To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

RAG genes encode the tissue‐specific components of VDJ recombination, that RAG‐2 is the key regulatory component, and that VDJ recom binase activity is regulated by transcriptional control elements in the target V gene segment.

the RAG-1 gene encodes the catalytic component of VDJ recom binase, and that RAG-2 gene encodes a regulatory component that controls VDJ recombin ase activity in a manner that is dependent upon the transcriptional activity of the target V gene segment.

RAG-2 is the lymphocyte-specific component of VDJ recombi-nase and is required for lymphocyte development, whereas RAG-1 is expressed in many tissues and is required for VDJ recombination in lymphocytes but not in any other cell type.

the mechanisms that control the expression and activity of VDJ recombination enzymes in lymphocytes.
understanding the function of the RAG proteins in the process of VDJ recombination.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control the initiation and termination of lymphocyte-specific VDJ recombination.
